title: Clinical management of rare brain tumor entities: A retrospective observational study
summary: This study aims to investigate how rare brain and spinal cord tumors have been treated at Heidelberg University Hospital over the past years. To do this, we will analyze existing routine medical data from patients who were diagnosed and treated between 2000 and 2024. The goal is to better understand which treatments were used, how effective they were, and what side effects occurred. The findings will help improve care for future patients. No new tests or treatments will be performed, and all data will be pseudonymized and handled in compliance with data protection regulations.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of spinal cord, cranial nerves and other parts of central nervous system
Secondary malignant neoplasm of brain and cerebral meninges
Secondary malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of nervous system

interventions.name: Patients with rare primary or secondary CNS tumors treated between 2000 and 2024 at Heidelberg University Hospital; retrospective analysis of routine clinical data without intervention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients with primary or secondary CNS tumors (ICD-10: C71.-, C72.-, C79.3, C79.4) whose data were available between January 1, 2000, and May 21, 2025, at the Department of Neurology, Heidelberg University Hospital.
Exclusion criteria:
No specific exclusion criteria; only incomplete datasets may be excluded if necessary.
